slides.title: Available customization

cards.title: Any browser framework
cards.body: The overlay implementation uses DOM/TypeScript rather than React.

cards.title: Lifecycle contract
cards.body: Await ready, subscribe deliberately and destroy on unmount.

cards.title: Two integration levels
cards.body: Direct overlay for a container; manager for floating widgets.

slides.notes: Customization comes from the current exports and prop declarations. Framework-independent: The overlay implementation uses DOM/TypeScript rather than React. Lifecycle contract: Await ready, subscribe deliberately and destroy on unmount. Two integration levels: Direct overlay for a container; manager for floating widgets. For UI, import the package stylesheet and use documented props or stable public classes. A component-level color override and inherited theme tokens are different levels of control. Locale strings and direction should be supplied by the host; do not introduce app i18n into a reusable library.

slides.title: Constraints that affect integration

cards.title: Embedding policy
cards.body: The server must allow the host origin in frame-ancestors.

cards.title: Auth constraints
cards.body: Provider iframe behavior varies; configure supported login UI modes.

cards.title: No server replacement
cards.body: The overlay still needs a running chat and backend.

slides.notes: Review these constraints before choosing the library. Embedding policy: The server must allow the host origin in frame-ancestors. Auth constraints: Provider iframe behavior varies; configure supported login UI modes. No server replacement: The overlay still needs a running chat and backend. The package is private in this snapshot. The presence of build/publish tooling is not evidence that a compatible release is available from a registry.
